content: Hahnemann University Hospital, founded in 1885, is located in Center City, Philadelphia. It is affiliated with Drexel University College of Medicine and serves as the Center City Hahnemann campus for the university. In 1993, Hahnemann University Hospital was purchased by Allegheny General. The following year, in 1994, the Woman's Medical College of Pennsylvania and the Medical College of Pennsylvania merged to create the MCP Hahnemann School of Medicine, which became part of the Allegheny University of the Health Sciences. However, in 1998, the parent organization of Allegheny University of the Health Sciences, the Allegheny Health Education and Research Foundation, filed for bankruptcy. Subsequently, Tenet Healthcare Corporation acquired the bankrupt Allegheny University and its associated assets, which included Hahnemann University Hospital as well as other regional hospitals such as Roxborough Memorial Hospital, St. Christopher’s Hospital for Children, and Warminster Hospital. After acquiring these assets, Tenet Healthcare established MCP Hahnemann University and entered into an agreement with Drexel University to manage its operations. In 2002, Tenet Healthcare finalized an arrangement for MCP Hahnemann University to be integrated into Drexel University for a 20-year period. As part of this agreement, Tenet also established an affiliation between Drexel University College of Medicine and Tenet's teaching hospitals in the Philadelphia region, with Hahnemann University Hospital being one of the key institutions involved in this partnership.
